Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres — Nxeon hosting platform), a real git repo with remote `origin`.

FIRST STEP, before any other work: this platform has a standing rule — NEVER build/run dev servers/run `npm run build` in the live prod tree `/opt/nxeon` or the shared staging tree `/opt/nxeon-staging` (a past agent clobbering `.next` there broke production). So start by creating your own isolated git worktree:
```
cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wip-domain-wizard -b feature/domain-wizard-address-phone-payment
cd /opt/nxeon-wip-domain-wizard && npm install
```
Do ALL reading, editing, building, and testing inside `/opt/nxeon-wip-domain-wizard` from that point on. Never write to `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging` directly.

GOAL: real, working improvements to the domain-registration wizard (`components/customer/DomainRegisterWizard.tsx`, action in `lib/actions-domains.ts`, page `app/dashboard/domains/register/page.tsx`). "Real" means actually functioning end-to-end, not a cosmetic mock — this codebase's established bar (see the comments throughout `lib/actions-domains.ts` about idempotency, no-blind-refund, verify-before-refund) is very high for anything that touches money or a registrar call. Match that bar; do not weaken any existing safety property while refactoring.

Four parts. Do them in this order (each depends conceptually on understanding the wizard's current step machine, so read `DomainRegisterWizard.tsx` and `lib/actions-domains.ts` fully before writing any code):

## Part 1 — Phone number input with country code, flag, and search

Replace the current free-text phone field (Contact step, validated against `PHONE_RE = /^\+\d{1,3}\.\d{4,14}$/`, format `+1.5551234567`) with a real international phone input: a country selector (searchable dropdown, flag shown via CSS/emoji — no new image assets, no external icon CDN — Unicode regional-indicator emoji flags derived from the ISO-3166 alpha-2 code work fine and need no asset pipeline) plus a national-number field. Use `libphonenumber-js` for parsing/formatting/validation (check if it's already a dependency; if not, add it — it's a small, dependency-light, widely-used library, not a paid service). The final value must still serialize to the exact `+<countrycode>.<number>` format the server-side zod schema in `lib/actions-domains.ts` (`purchaseDomain`) expects — don't change that wire format, build the picker as a client-side affordance on top of it. Validate for real (a genuinely invalid number for the selected country should block continuing), not just format-shape matching.

Build a reusable `components/customer/PhoneCountryInput.tsx` (or similar) — check if anything phone-related already exists in `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx` (has some phone handling per a repo search) before writing a new one from scratch; reuse if it already does most of this.

## Part 2 — Real address lookup/validation (Geoapify)

The owner chose **Geoapify** (its free tier is fine for commercial/business use, not residential-only — already confirmed). No API key exists yet in this environment. Build the integration gated on a `GEOAPIFY_API_KEY` env var, following this codebase's established graceful-degradation convention (see how `freeInboxPlan` being `null` makes the wizard's Email step simply not render, never claiming a feature that isn't provisioned — same idea here): when the key is absent, the address fields stay exactly as today (plain text inputs, no autocomplete) — the feature must not break, error, or look broken on an environment without the key.

When the key IS present:
- Add a small server route (e.g. `app/api/geoapify/autocomplete/route.ts`) that proxies Geoapify's Autocomplete API server-side (never expose the API key to the client bundle) — rate-limit/debounce-friendly, takes a partial address query string and optional country-bias, returns normalized suggestions.
- Wire the Contact step's Street address field to a debounced autocomplete dropdown (same UX shape as the existing domain-search autocomplete already in this same wizard — reuse that debounce/dropdown pattern, don't invent a new one) that, on selection, fills address1/city/stateProvince/postalCode/country from the chosen suggestion.
- Also validate the manually-typed case (someone who ignores the dropdown and just types): a light server-side check via Geoapify's geocoding response confidence/match-type, used only to flag ("we couldn't verify this address — check for typos") not to hard-block, since ICANN registrant-contact fields are the source of truth, not Geoapify's.
- Add `GEOAPIFY_API_KEY=` to `.env.example` if one exists (do NOT put a real key anywhere — there isn't one yet; the owner will add the real value to the live `.env` themselves).

## Part 3 — Card payment for domain purchases (currently wallet-only, blocks anyone without wallet funds)

This is the highest-stakes part — a real money path touching a real registrar API call. Read ALL of `lib/actions-domains.ts`'s `purchaseDomain` function first; it has extensive, deliberate safety logic (idempotency guard, in-transaction duplicate check, `verifyRegistration()` before any refund decision, three-way registered/not-registered/unknown outcome handling with the "unknown → never auto-refund, flag for manual review" rule). Every one of these properties MUST be preserved.

Mirror the existing wallet+card-split checkout pattern used for VPS/game orders — read these as your reference implementation, in this order:
- `lib/stripe.ts`: `createOrderPaymentSession` (VPS card leg) and `createGameOrderPaymentSession` (game analogue) — the pattern is: card charges only the *shortfall* between wallet balance and total, that gets credited to the customer's wallet via Stripe fulfilment, then a `place*Order` function debits the wallet for the FROZEN price captured at checkout-session-creation time (never re-quoted later — this codebase calls a stale re-quote "the H2 incident" and treats avoiding it as load-bearing).
- `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`: `runFulfilment()`'s dispatch — see the `order` branch (~line 236) and `gameOrder` branch for the claim/settle/notify/reportPurchase shape you need to add a `domainOrder` branch alongside.
- `lib/stripe.ts`: `classifyCheckoutSession()` — add a branch recognizing new domain-order metadata keys, following the existing keys' naming convention (`nxeonOrder`, `nxeonOrderPrice`, etc. → use `nxeonDomainOrder` / `nxeonDomainOrderPrice`).
- `components/customer/PaymentStep.tsx` and how `DeployWizard.tsx` embeds it as a wizard step gated on wallet shortfall — reuse this exact component/pattern for the domain wizard's Review step rather than building a new payment UI (the owner explicitly asked to mirror "the wizard work we did", i.e. this same Payment-step + Custom-Checkout-Elements pattern already proven in `AddFundsPaymentModal.tsx`/`PaymentStep.tsx`).

Concretely: extract `purchaseDomain`'s core registration logic (the registrar call + wallet debit + `Domain` row create/update + verify-on-failure + `setupDomainInboxEmail` call) into a shared function parameterized by a FROZEN price (not a fresh quote), callable both from the existing direct-wallet server action and from a new fulfilment path. Add `createDomainOrderPaymentSession()` in `lib/stripe.ts` for the card leg. Update the wizard's Review step: when wallet balance < total, show the embedded Payment step (card covers the shortfall) instead of just blocking with "Insufficient balance"; when balance already covers it, keep today's one-click wallet-only registration exactly as is (don't force a card step on people who don't need one).

Do NOT touch anything related to VM root passwords, SSH keys, or other server credentials — out of scope and irrelevant here; mentioned only so you don't wander into that territory while reading shared files.

## Part 4 — Post-purchase "provisioning" animation

The owner wants the same full-screen deploy animation used for VPS/game-server provisioning to show after a domain purchase completes. Read `components/customer/ProvisioningOverlay.tsx` in full — it's already generic enough to reuse as-is (productLabel/hostname/status/transitional/justPaid/readyStatus/etc. are all props, no VPS-specific logic hardcoded). Domain registration is synchronous (the server action itself calls the registrar and only redirects on success/failure — there's no async job to poll), so the relevant branch is the one already built for "sandbox mode completes instantly": `justPaid && status === readyStatus` shows a brief provisioning phase (floored at `MIN_PROVISIONING_MS`) then flips to a success card — exactly the effect wanted here.

Mount `<ProvisioningOverlay>` on `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx`. That page already reads `?new=1` (`justRegistered`) and computes `showGoLive = justRegistered === "1" && active` for an existing upsell banner — reuse that same signal as the `justPaid` prop (don't invent a second query param). Map props sensibly: `productLabel="domain"`, `hostname={domain.name}`, `status={domain.status}`, `transitional={domain.status === "PENDING"}`, `readyStatus="ACTIVE"`, `connectAddress=null`, `planName` = something like `"${termYears}-year registration"`, `osName=null`, `rootPassword=null`, `extraInfo` = the free-inbox mailbox address as a row if one was set up (check `lib/domain-inbox-email.ts` for how to look that up), `dashboardHref` = the domain's own detail page URL. This overlay and the existing go-live banner should coexist fine (overlay is dismissable, banner stays underneath) — don't remove or fight the existing banner.

## Standing rules for this repo (non-negotiable)

- **Any Prisma schema change must be written as a migration file for human review — you must NEVER run `prisma migrate deploy`/`db push` or otherwise apply it yourself.** If you find you need a schema change for any part above, stop, write the migration SQL file, and clearly flag it in your final report as "NOT APPLIED — needs manual review" rather than running it.
- **Never rotate, regenerate, or touch any live credential** (API keys, passwords, tokens) on any real infrastructure. This task shouldn't require it, but if you find yourself about to, stop and flag it instead.
- Match the codebase's existing comment style: comments explain non-obvious WHY (a past incident, a subtle invariant), never WHAT. Don't over-comment new code.
- No new UI dependencies beyond `libphonenumber-js` (Part 1) unless something is truly unavoidable — flag any other new dependency clearly in your report rather than silently adding it.

## Verification (all required before you report done)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full test suite (`npm test`), diffed by exact failing-test-name against a fresh run on `main` in the same worktree — zero NEW failures (there are pre-existing unrelated failures in this repo already; matching that exact same set is the bar, not zero total failures).
3. Add/extend tests for Part 3's money-path logic specifically — at minimum: a frozen-price fulfilment test (price at checkout-creation time is what gets charged even if a live quote would differ later), and a test that the wallet+card split math matches the existing VPS/game order tests' shape.
4. Commit your work on the `feature/domain-wizard-address-phone-payment` branch inside the worktree (do not push, do not open a PR, do not merge to main — that's for the platform owner to review). Do NOT deploy anywhere or attempt to promote to staging/production.

Report back with: a summary of what was built per part, the exact list of changed/added files, the migration file path if Part 2/3 needed one (flagged NOT APPLIED), confirmation of tsc+test results, the worktree path and branch name, and anything you deliberately left out of scope or need a decision on (e.g. exact visual placement of the new phone/address fields, since that's a product/UX call not a technical one).

6	/**

8	 * this; when the natural remainder would fall under it we leave exactly this
9	 * much on the card and apply slightly less wallet credit (see walletSplit).
10	 */
11	export const STRIPE_MIN_CENTS = 50;
12	
13	export type WalletSplit = {
14	  /** Cents taken from the customer's existing wallet balance. */
15	  walletApplied: number;
16	  /** Cents charged to the card (0 = fully paid from wallet, no Stripe). */
17	  cardCents: number;
18	  /** True when we bumped the card up to STRIPE_MIN_CENTS (reducing wallet). */
19	  clampedForStripeMin: boolean;
20	  /**
21	   * True when the WHOLE amount due is under Stripe's floor, so no card leg exists
22	   * at all and `walletApplied` is the entire due (see walletSplit). Distinct from
23	   * `clampedForStripeMin`, which means the opposite thing — that a card leg does
24	   * exist and was raised to the floor. Surfaces must not conflate them: the deploy
25	   * wizard's `clampedForStripeMin` line says "we'll charge {cardCents} to your
26	   * card", which would be a flat lie here, where `cardCents` is 0.
27	   *
28	   * In this state `walletApplied` may EXCEED the customer's balance. That is not a
29	   * claim the balance covers it — it is the amount that must come from the wallet
30	   * because nothing else can settle it. The caller's guarded `debitWallet` decides
31	   * whether it succeeds, and a surface showing this flag should tell the customer
32	   * to top up rather than imply the payment is already funded.
33	   */
34	  belowStripeMin: boolean;
35	};
36	
37	/**
38	 * Split a due amount between the wallet and the card, honoring the customer's
39	 * "apply my balance" toggle and Stripe's minimum-charge floor.
40	 *
41	 * - `useWallet` off  → everything on the card.
42	 * - wallet covers all → cardCents = 0 (caller pays entirely from wallet, no Stripe).
43	 * - partial cover     → walletApplied = min(balance, due), card = the remainder.
44	 * - tiny remainder    → if 0 < card < STRIPE_MIN_CENTS, reduce walletApplied so
45	 *   exactly STRIPE_MIN_CENTS lands on the card (never send Stripe a sub-minimum
46	 *   charge). Integer-cent exact throughout.
47	 * - whole due sub-floor → no card leg is possible at all; the wallet takes it all
48	 *   and `belowStripeMin` is set (see below).
49	 *
50	 * POSTCONDITION, relied on by every caller: `cardCents` is either 0 or at least
51	 * STRIPE_MIN_CENTS. `lib/actions-server.ts` and `lib/actions-disk.ts` hand
52	 * `cardCents` straight to `createResizeCheckout` / `createDiskExpandCheckout`,
53	 * which guard only `cardCents <= 0` — a sub-floor positive amount reached

55	 * fixed HERE, in the one function that owns the floor, rather than by bolting a
56	 * duplicate guard onto each call site.
57	 */

59	  dueCents: number;
60	  balanceCents: number;
61	  useWallet: boolean;
62	}): WalletSplit {
63	  const dueCents = Math.max(0, Math.round(opts.dueCents));
64	  const balanceCents = Math.max(0, Math.round(opts.balanceCents));
65	  if (dueCents <= 0) {
66	    return { walletApplied: 0, cardCents: 0, clampedForStripeMin: false, belowStripeMin: false };
67	  }
68	
69	  // The whole amount due is under Stripe's floor, so there is no card leg to be
70	  // had: the clamp below works by moving cents from the wallet ONTO the card, and
71	  // here there are not enough cents in the charge to reach the floor no matter how
72	  // they are divided. Previously this fell through and returned whatever sub-floor
73	  // remainder was left (due 30, balance 10 -> cardCents 20), which Stripe rejects.
74	  //
75	  // Two behaviours were available and only one is honest. Inflating the card leg to
76	  // 50c would charge the customer more than they owe. So the card is dropped
77	  // entirely and the wallet takes the whole amount — the only leg that can settle
78	  // a 30c charge — REGARDLESS of `useWallet`, because respecting that preference
79	  // here would mean no payable split exists at all. `belowStripeMin` reports it so
80	  // callers and surfaces state what happened instead of implying a funded card
81	  // payment, and when the balance falls short the caller's guarded `debitWallet`
82	  // fails with the actionable "top up your wallet first" rather than a Stripe API
83	  // error. Note walletApplied + cardCents === dueCents still holds exactly.
84	  if (dueCents < STRIPE_MIN_CENTS) {
85	    return { walletApplied: dueCents, cardCents: 0, clampedForStripeMin: false, belowStripeMin: true };
86	  }
87	
88	  let walletApplied = opts.useWallet ? Math.min(balanceCents, dueCents) : 0;
89	  let cardCents = dueCents - walletApplied;
90	  let clampedForStripeMin = false;
91	
92	  // A tiny non-zero card remainder that Stripe would reject. This only happens
93	  // when the wallet can't cover the whole charge (otherwise cardCents === 0), so
94	  // the least-surprising fix is to leave STRIPE_MIN_CENTS on the card and apply a
95	  // touch less wallet. `dueCents >= STRIPE_MIN_CENTS` is guaranteed by the early
96	  // return above, so walletApplied can never go negative here.
97	  if (cardCents > 0 && cardCents < STRIPE_MIN_CENTS) {
98	    walletApplied = dueCents - STRIPE_MIN_CENTS;
99	    cardCents = STRIPE_MIN_CENTS;
100	    clampedForStripeMin = true;
101	  }
102	  return { walletApplied, cardCents, clampedForStripeMin, belowStripeMin: false };
103	}
